newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian opposition leader says he's being framed.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian opposition leader says he's being framed.

text.p: Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy on Wednesday accused co-Premier Hun Sen of trying to destroy his reputation by arresting a member of his Khmer Nation Party (KNP) on murder charges.
Police on Monday charged three people, including KNP steering committee member and security chief Srung Vong Vannak, of suspected involvement in the murder of Hun Sen's brother-in-law last year.
Sam Rainsy said he feared the arrest of the three men was the first step in a bid to implicate him in personally ordering the killing of Hun Sen's brother-in-law, Keov Samuth, 39.

"Hun Sen is trying to destabilise (us)... The stage is set to make Sam Rainsy another Sirivudh, because Sirivudh was accused of trying to kill Hun Sen, and Sam Rainsy will be accused of having ordered the assassination of Hun Sen's brother-in-law," said Sam Rainsy.
Prince Norodom Sirivudh, a former foreign minister, was exiled to France in 1995 for allegedly plotting to kill Hun Sen.
Keov Samuth, a senior Interior Ministry police official, was gunned down outside a Phnom Penh restaurant on November 19 in what was widely seen as a political attack.
On Monday, the three suspects were charged in connection with the murder and ordered remanded in custody for further investigations, court officials and police said on Wednesday.

Chief of Penal Police Mok Chito said one of the suspects, Sokha Sim, surrendered to police early last month and confessed to the killing, alleging to police that he had been hired by the two others held this week.
When Keov Samuth was killed, Hun Sen said he believed the murder was linked to the defection of a group of Khmer Rouge underground agents in the capital.

The alleged defectors accused Sam Rainsy of receiving funds from the Khmer Rouge, who had been fighting the current coalition after reneging on a 1991 peace pact. The Maoist group's brutal 1975-79 rule killed more than one million people.

Hostility between Sam Rainsy and Hun Sen has grown in recent months, especially since Sam Rainsy, a former finance minister, joined co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh in a political coalition ahead of elections planned for 1998.
Although Ranariddh is Hun Sen's partner in Cambodia's ruling coalition government, the two are also fierce political rivals.
